title: WebMCP and Graph OS production readiness

baseline.evidence_scope: repository only; live deployment, legal identity, DNS, analytics property, and browser origin trial are unverified

current_working_tree_evidence.scope: Targeted receipts from the current working tree; these are partial implementation evidence and do not close requirements or release gates.

receipts.proves: Static asset checks pass in safe noindex mode.
Image-alt scan passes for 167 TSX source files.
Eight targeted files and 30 tests pass for route head/metadata, public/mobile surfaces, consent/analytics, responsive behavior, site-config gating, and image behavior.
Seven missing or invalid deployment/legal values are rejected: origin, owner, contact address, effective date, legal revision, privacy text, and terms text.

The live app route enforces authentication, exact same origin, bounded control-safe fields and envelope, fixed destination and retention, local defense-in-depth throttling, required atomic idempotency and shared-limiter adapter capabilities, a server deadline, strict results, success-only durable contact-namespaced receipts, and response privacy.

The contact form preserves input on refusal, exposes accessible field/summary and pending states, enforces a bounded client deadline and unmount cancellation, coalesces duplicate clicks, reuses its idempotency key on retry, shares exact receipt validation with the thank-you page, and stores a validated receipt before the real App route navigates.

still_open: Graph OS bridge authority and server-verified identity/session/tenant/principal/document/route/generation binding
attended opt-in, at-most-once fences, honest cancellation effects, durable audit before dispatch, one BrowserControlService, and truthful Langfuse status
real owner-supplied legal/contact values and the production governed contact adapter
configured analytics destination, anonymous SSO policy, and deployed-topology receipts
general form-error sweep and deployed contact delivery receipt

overview: Govern the boundary between browser-local WebMCP controls and Graph OS remote MCP while making the WebUI production-ready through one route metadata authority, shared public/legal layout, shared consent and analytics loader, existing loading/error primitives, and one image policy.

user_stories.action: use one policy and provenance envelope across WebUI, MCP, REST, and WebMCP projections
user_stories.value: a UI path cannot bypass authorization or create an untraceable execution

user_stories.value: the product is usable and safe in production

allows: local Atlas filter and selection state
browser_local_webmcp.active_registration_generation: provider derives a local registration key from identity/page context, but no server-verified generation is currently bound to a Graph OS lease or call

governed_remote_mcp.transport: same-origin WebUI backend routes to the Graph OS gateway

leased_browser_bridge.authority: Graph OS BrowserControlService owns authorization, leases, replay/fence state, call state, durable audit, receipts, and terminal outcomes; WebUI only transports and presents them
leased_browser_bridge.contract: short-lived opaque capability lease bound to server-verified login session, principal, tenant, session/device, origin, document, route, active registration generation, policy, tool versions, attended opt-in, nonce/fence, cancellation, truthful Langfuse status, and RunTrace

audit_defects.title: No shared capability descriptor for browser-local and remote authorities
audit_defects.required_disposition: Publish one versioned descriptor that labels authority without merging execution paths.

audit_defects.title: Route metadata does not cover head, CTA, indexability, or WebMCP identity
audit_defects.required_disposition: Extend the route registry once and derive route head, CTA, mobile, page context, and WebMCP identity.

audit_defects.title: No user-bound Graph OS to browser capability lease lifecycle
audit_defects.required_disposition: Implement issue, renew, revoke, expiry, and browser-channel binding through the server-mediated lease authority.

audit_defects.title: No shared provenance, Langfuse, or RunTrace envelope for WebMCP calls
audit_defects.required_disposition: Create an immutable call receipt with actor, route, lease, schema digest, policy, timing, result or error digest, and trace IDs.

audit_defects.title: Cancellation exists locally but not across a remote bridge
audit_defects.required_disposition: Make cancellation, expiry, disconnect, timeout, replay, and late-result behavior idempotent end to end; prevent new uncorrelated dispatch, report the honest effect state, and reconcile committed or unknown effects without unconditional late-effect rejection.

audit_defects.title: No canonical control-operation and mutation-confirmation mapping
audit_defects.required_disposition: Reuse one Graph OS control operation and policy decision for REST, MCP, and WebMCP projections; require exact-request confirmation for mutation.

audit_defects.title: No deployed-topology proof for WebMCP browser prerequisites and bridge failure-closed behavior
audit_defects.required_disposition: Add static, browser, integration, and deployed-topology receipts for secure context, Permissions Policy, origin-trial absence, identity, lease, and telemetry.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: Active registration generation
adversarial_review_requirements.description: Each active document/tool set has a server-verifiable registration_generation bound to document, route, identity, and tool/schema digest; old generations are refused.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: Graph OS owns bridge authority
adversarial_review_requirements.description: Graph OS solely owns authorization, leases, replay/fence state, call state, durable audit receipts, and terminal outcomes; WebUI has no shadow authority.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: Server-verified login/session binding
adversarial_review_requirements.description: Every lease and call verifies live login session, tenant, principal, origin, document, route, and active registration generation from server state.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: Attended opt-in
adversarial_review_requirements.description: Remote browser control requires an explicit attended visible UI gesture for the current session, visible scope, and revoke; hidden or unattended renewal is refused.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: At-most-once dispatch fence
adversarial_review_requirements.description: Graph OS persists a durable call fence/state before dispatch and retries or duplicate protocol deliveries cannot dispatch a browser side effect more than once.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: Service credentials are not user delegation
adversarial_review_requirements.description: A service credential authenticates a service only and is never treated as proof that a human delegated browser control.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: Honest cancellation effect state
adversarial_review_requirements.description: Cancellation reports exactly one of none, browser_reported_committed, or unknown; it does not claim rollback or unconditional late-effect rejection.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: One BrowserControlService
adversarial_review_requirements.description: Graph OS MCP, REST, and workflow adapters all call one BrowserControlService for browser authorization, dispatch, confirmation, cancellation, fences, and receipts.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: Durable audit before dispatch
adversarial_review_requirements.description: Actor, lease, policy, call fence, requested tool, generation, and pending receipt are durably persisted before any browser command; audit failure prevents dispatch.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: Truthful Langfuse status
adversarial_review_requirements.description: Receipts distinguish recorded, not_configured, and unavailable Langfuse status and never fabricate a trace ID or recorded state.

adversarial_review_requirements.title: Trust prerequisite gate
adversarial_review_requirements.description: The remote bridge is disabled unless secure context/Permissions Policy, authenticated channel, verified login/session/tenant/principal, document/route/generation, attended opt-in, healthy Graph OS lease authority, policy digest, and durable audit path exist.

deduplication_policies.name: loading-error-primitives
deduplication_policies.owner: existing route fallback, ErrorBoundary, Skeleton, UnavailableNotice, SessionExpiredNotice, and form validation primitives

deduplication_policies.name: image-policy
deduplication_policies.owner: one asset and JSX image policy

functional_requirements.title: Custom 404 page
functional_requirements.description: Unknown routes render an accessible custom 404 with safe navigation and no fabricated data; direct requests preserve a real 404 where the serving topology supports it.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown route renders a route-registry-backed 404 title, description, heading, and safe CTA.
The page does not fall through to a plausible application page or fabricate data.
Direct navigation and SPA navigation have documented status behavior.

functional_requirements.title: Meta title on every page
functional_requirements.description: Every route has a deterministic unique document title, including 404, thank-you, privacy, and terms, and route transitions update it.
acceptance_criteria: Every route descriptor has a title template or explicit title.
Head updates occur on route changes without a full reload.
No route falls back to the same generic title except an explicitly documented error state.

functional_requirements.title: Meta description on every page
functional_requirements.description: Every public/indexable route has a specific description and private routes have safe noindex metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Public route descriptions are present, bounded, and route-specific.
Private application routes are noindex and do not expose sensitive context in metadata.
A metadata test covers every route-registry entry.

functional_requirements.title: CTA above the fold
functional_requirements.description: Each public entry or landing page exposes one keyboard-accessible primary CTA above the fold from route metadata.
acceptance_criteria: CTA target, role requirement, and sanitized analytics event are declared once.
The CTA is visible without scrolling at the defined desktop and mobile viewports.
A CTA never promises an action unavailable to the current actor.

functional_requirements.title: Favicon set
functional_requirements.description: The built artifact serves the complete branded favicon and manifest set from one asset source.
acceptance_criteria: ICO, SVG/PNG variants, Apple touch icon, manifest, and theme metadata are linked and load successfully.
Links are generated from the same versioned asset policy.
Missing or stale assets fail the static asset gate.

functional_requirements.title: robots.txt
functional_requirements.description: Environment-aware robots policy disallows private paths and advertises the sitemap only in an indexable environment.
acceptance_criteria: Private/authenticated/control-plane paths are disallowed.
Sitemap URL is emitted only for the canonical indexable host.
Preview and local environments do not accidentally invite indexing.

functional_requirements.title: sitemap.xml
functional_requirements.description: Generated sitemap contains only public canonical route-registry entries without IDs, query strings, or fragments.
acceptance_criteria: Every sitemap URL is public, canonical, and indexable.
No private route, object ID, session identifier, query, or fragment is present.
Sitemap generation fails on a public route missing canonical metadata.

functional_requirements.title: Open Graph image
functional_requirements.description: Shareable public routes expose safe Open Graph/Twitter metadata and one versioned compressed image; private routes expose no user or graph data.
acceptance_criteria: OG image, dimensions, absolute URL, type, and alt metadata validate.
Private routes are noindex and do not include private content in social metadata.
The asset satisfies FR-020 compression checks.

functional_requirements.title: Alt text on every image
functional_requirements.description: Every meaningful image has contextual alt text and every decorative image has explicit decorative semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Static checks cover all JSX image elements and generated image components.
Decorative images use empty alt and appropriate presentation semantics.
Image load failure and lazy states remain understandable to assistive technology.

functional_requirements.title: Mobile breakpoints
functional_requirements.description: Every route declares truthful mobile behavior and supported/adapted routes pass a viewport matrix without inaccessible overflow or clipped controls.
acceptance_criteria: Every route has full, adapted, or unsupported behavior in the route registry.
Full/adapted routes pass the supported viewport matrix with no horizontal overflow.
Unsupported routes explain the limitation and offer a safe alternative.

functional_requirements.title: Sticky mobile CTA
functional_requirements.description: Public mobile flows with a primary CTA use one shared sticky treatment that respects focus, safe areas, zoom, reduced motion, and content overlap.
acceptance_criteria: The shared component is driven by route metadata and is not copied per page.
Keyboard focus and screen-reader order remain correct when the CTA becomes sticky.
Viewport safe-area and reduced-motion behavior are tested.

functional_requirements.title: Loading states
functional_requirements.description: Every lazy route, data request, WebMCP catalog, lease operation, and submission exposes an accessible loading state using shared primitives.
acceptance_criteria: Loading is distinct from empty, unavailable, denied, cancelled, and success.
Duplicate submissions are prevented where the operation is not idempotent.
No loading path renders fabricated data or a success toast.

functional_requirements.title: Form error states
functional_requirements.description: Forms expose field and summary errors, accessible invalid state, preserved safe input, honest server/network failure, and no secret echo.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid fields expose aria-invalid and descriptions.
Server, validation, network, and cancellation errors have distinct user-facing states.
Sensitive input and raw backend traces never appear in error text.

functional_requirements.title: Thank-you page
functional_requirements.description: Confirmed contact or CTA submission navigates to a dedicated metadata-backed thank-you page with a bounded receipt and next-step CTA.
acceptance_criteria: The page is a route-registry entry using the public/legal layout.
The URL contains no PII or raw submission data.
The page is shown only after backend confirmation and does not claim delivery on failure.

functional_requirements.title: Privacy policy page
functional_requirements.description: A reviewed public privacy page identifies the controller, purposes, data categories, retention, processors, choices, security contact, effective date, and revision.
acceptance_criteria: The page uses the shared public/legal layout and route metadata.
Legal owner review and effective/revision metadata are attached to the release receipt.
Placeholder or missing legal identity blocks release.

functional_requirements.title: Terms and conditions
functional_requirements.description: A reviewed public terms page contains service terms, acceptable use, agent-control boundaries, disclaimers, governing/contact information, effective date, and revision.
acceptance_criteria: The page uses the shared public/legal layout and route metadata.
Agent, MCP, WebMCP, and user-control boundaries are explicit.
Placeholder or missing legal identity blocks release.

functional_requirements.title: Cookie banner
functional_requirements.description: Nonessential cookies/storage are blocked until affirmative versioned consent through one accessible, reversible consent surface.
acceptance_criteria: Analytics/marketing storage is absent before consent and after revoke.
Necessary authentication/session cookies are distinguished from optional categories.
Consent state is versioned, region/configuration aware, and does not collect unnecessary identity data.

functional_requirements.title: Analytics installed
functional_requirements.description: Analytics loads through the shared consent-aware loader with a configured property or truthful disabled state and emits only sanitized events.
acceptance_criteria: No nonessential analytics request occurs before consent.
Events omit prompts, tool arguments, graph contents, tokens, secrets, and sensitive query values.
Server Langfuse/RunTrace operational tracing remains separate from marketing/product analytics.

functional_requirements.title: Real contact address
functional_requirements.description: Legal, contact, thank-you, and consent surfaces use a verified owner-supplied contact address; missing, sample, or invented values block release.
acceptance_criteria: The address is supplied through reviewed configuration/content and is not invented by implementation.
Privacy, terms, and consent pages display the same verified value.
A placeholder detector fails the release gate.

functional_requirements.title: Compressed images
functional_requirements.description: All shipped raster, favicon, Open Graph, and user-upload image assets satisfy one format, dimension, byte-budget, compression, cache, and fallback policy.
acceptance_criteria: Static assets pass the declared dimensions, formats, byte limits, and compression checks.
Open Graph and favicon assets use the same policy.
User uploads are validated and bounded before persistence or display.

bridge_acceptance.description: Supported browsers register only bounded browser-local tools; unsupported or insecure contexts remain a typed no-op.
Capability catalogs label browser-local, WebUI-BFF, and Graph OS remote authority with tool/schema/version/role, mutation/confirmation, and active registration-generation metadata.
Graph OS lease issuance verifies live login session, actor/principal, route, tenant, origin, document, active generation, attended opt-in, and role policy and cannot cross those bindings.
A leased read-only call reaches only the named local tool, returns bounded schema-valid output, and produces one receipt.
Mutating browser control requires exact-request user confirmation and stale or denied leases never reach the action.

No browser request, tool payload, error, analytics, Langfuse, or RunTrace field contains a service bearer, Keycloak token, OpenBao value, or unredacted secret; a service credential is never user delegation.

Identity change, sign-out, route or generation change, tenant change, expiry, cancel, timeout, and disconnect are idempotent; terminal effect is none, browser_reported_committed, or unknown without claiming rollback or unconditional late-effect rejection.

Graph OS durably audits before dispatch and preserves verified session/actor/tenant/principal/document/route/generation, lease, policy, nonce/fence, timing, result/error, cancellation effect, RunTrace, and truthful Langfuse status for every outcome.
WebMCP, REST, MCP, and workflow projections use one Graph OS BrowserControlService and authorization decision.

Browser, integration, and deployed-topology tests cover secure context, Permissions Policy, origin-trial absence, deep links, route/generation changes, attended opt-in, mobile, restart/reconnect, replay fences, and trust-prerequisite refusal.

non_functional_requirements: NFR-005 no duplicated authorities or policy surfaces

verification.release_rule: All open WMCP audit defects, ADV-001..ADV-011, FR-001..FR-020, BR-001..BR-010, NFR-001..NFR-007, and constitution gates must have green evidence; spec creation alone is not implementation.
